{{Infobox academic|name=Adolé Glitho-Akueson|birth_name=Adolé Isabelle Glitho-Akueson|birth_place=Cove, Benin|birth_date={{Birth date and age|1949|05|04|df=yes}}|citizenship=Togo|occupation=Professor of Animal Biology|discipline=Entomology|sub_discipline=Medical and horticultural entomology}}'''Adolé Isabelle Glitho-Akueson''' (born 4 May 1949) is a [[Togo]]lese entomologist who is Professor of Animal Biology at the [[University of Lomé]]. She is the chair of UNESCO's "Women, Science and Sustainable Water Management in West Africa and Central Africa" committee and a Fellow of the [[African Academy of Sciences]].

== Biography ==
Glitho-Akueson was born on 4 May 1949 in [[Benin]]. She went to secondary school in Benin and also studied for her undergraduate degree there. In 1973 she moved to France to study at [[University of Burgundy|University of Dijon]], from where she was awarded her Masters in Animal Biology in 1975. She continued to study as was awarded her doctorate in Insect Physiology in 1977.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=African Union regional awards for scientific women "Kwame N'krumah " {{!}} Economic Community of West African States(ECOWAS)|url=https://www.ecowas.int/african-union-regional-awards-for-scientific-women-kwame-nkrumah/|access-date=2021-03-21|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-04-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421223501/https://www.ecowas.int/african-union-regional-awards-for-scientific-women-kwame-nkrumah/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 1978, she returned to West Africa and began her first academic post as assistant lecturer in Animal Biology in the Faculty of Sciences in [[University of Lomé]] in September 1978. In 1981, she was appointed to a full lectureship.<ref name=":1" /> In 1989 she awarded a scholarship, funded by the [[African Union]], to study [[Electron microscope|electron microscopy]] at the [[University of Tours]]. In 1992, she was appointed Assistant Professor in Animal Biology (specialty in Entomology) at the University of Lomé. In 1998 she was appointed to a full professorship.<ref name=":1" />

Glitho-Akueson was employed as a visiting fellow at the [[University of Tours|Universities of Tours]] (1993 - 2011), [[Abdou Moumouni University|Niamey]] and [[University of Ouagadougou|Ouagadougou]] (1990 - 2015).<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Afriscitech - Isabelle Glitho|url=https://www.afriscitech.com/en/isabelle-glitho|access-date=2021-03-23|website=www.afriscitech.com|archive-date=5 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210605180237/https://www.afriscitech.com/en/isabelle-glitho|url-status=dead}}</ref> Her expertise lies in the integrated management of pest populations.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|last=|date=2015-11-13|title=GLITHO-AKUESON|url=https://en.unesco.org/who-who-women-speakers/glitho-akueson|url-status=dead|access-date=2021-03-23|website=UNESCO|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210605180235/https://en.unesco.org/who-who-women-speakers/glitho-akueson |archive-date=2021-06-05 }}</ref>

She is a member of the advisory committee of the Sustainable Food Security for West and Central Africa (SADAOC) Foundation. She holds the UNESCO Chair "Women, Science and Sustainable Water Management in West Africa” and is an expert in access to higher education for women in Africa.<ref name=":3" /> She has published over 130 papers and has acted as international advisor on a number of large-scale global research programmes.<ref name=":0" /> She is the Vice-Président of Togolese National Academy of Science, Art and Letters (ANSALT) and a Fellow of the [[African Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=":2" />

== Awards ==
* Knight of CAMES Academic Palms<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Glitho-Akueson Isabelle {{!}} The AAS|url=https://www.aasciences.africa/fellow/glitho-akueson-isabelle|access-date=2021-03-14|website=www.aasciences.africa|archive-date=2021-06-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210605180237/https://www.aasciences.africa/fellow/glitho-akueson-isabelle|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* Knight of La Légion d’Honneur  (France)<ref name=":0" />
* Laureate for the Regional African Union [[Kwame Nkrumah]] Scientific Award  - 2013<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />
